title: Review of c45's sparse sink-escape finding (fresh seed 94, discs 1 per 200 t): replicated. mar-40 rods escape 10 of 12 caught (0.83) against 4 of 11 at mar 0 (0.36), few bodies are caught per run, and the selection gradient on distance per cycle is negative in the escape arm (-0.17 [-0.47, -0.10]) and near zero in the removal control (-0.05); Supported
summary: Re-ran the finding's world.py (identical to the dense-disc world, disc_dt 200 default) on fresh seed 94: arm S and arm I at mar 40 and arm S at mar 0, 128^2, T=1600, with c45's fate.py, c00's extract.py and c00's mtips.py. Escape share of bodies inside a disc's final radius one frame after it opened: 10/12 (0.83) at mar 40 vs 4/11 (0.36) at mar 0, 2.3x (c45: 0.86 and 0.60 vs 0.33), again with few caught bodies (11-12 per run, c45 3-7). Gradients of relative descendants on standardized D, speed, straightness: S D -0.17 [-0.47, -0.10], speed +0.02, straightness +0.18; I D -0.05 [-0.21, +0.17], straightness +0.35; mar 0 D -0.07. Median D of dividing rods S 1.09, I 1.56 rod lengths. Rear tip advancing >= 2/3 of net: 25 of 30 (S) and 28 of 30 (I) of mtips.py's dividing set. Persistent splits S 37, I 36, mar 0 31 (generation 4-6). The negative result (sparse discs do not make distance per cycle pay) reproduces.

observations.M: out/S_fate.txt escape 10/12 (0.83), D gradient -0.17 [-0.47, -0.10]; out/S_mar0_fate.txt escape 4/11 (0.36); out/I_fate.txt D gradient -0.05 [-0.21, +0.17]; out/S_tips.txt 25 of 30 dividing rods translate

seeds_run.result: pass: escape advantage and the non-positive D gradient reproduce

controls_run.M: rerun/I (removal at disc opening) and rerun/S_mar0 (drive off), seed 94

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; 11-12 caught bodies per run, so the escape shares carry wide binomial error; selection gradients rest on 22-26 dividing tracks.
